parts.note: Useful St James’s complaints contact and timings, but it misses that the formal national route is HSE Your Service Your Say and the key clinical-judgement exclusion.
Correctly points to the Ombudsman and basic prerequisites, but omits the clinical-judgement bar and did not reach the actual forms.ie complaint form.
Right that medical negligence goes to court and not IRB, with SCA handling covered public claims; wrong on the core limitation period, which is 2 years from date of knowledge, not 3.
Good Legal Aid Board coverage and calculator, but it is too hesitant on conditional fees: percentage-of-damages fees are banned, yet no-win-no-fee style arrangements can still exist.
Found the official Law Society search, but missed the important limitation that there is no clinical-negligence/specialism filter.
It identified guideline bodies/repositories, but missed the key answer: no Irish national scaphoid/fracture guideline was found, so UK guidance is only persuasive.
Correctly found the Patient Advocacy Service, but missed the actual online enquiry form and did not note that PAS is not legal/compensation advice.
Good St James’s records route and one-month timing, but it omits the usual SAR form + photo ID requirement and the general no-portal point.

smart: It correctly worked out that compensation is a clinical-negligence court claim and not an Injuries Resolution Board claim, and tied St James’s into the SCA/Clinical Indemnity Scheme route.
worst: It gives the wrong limitation period for the compensation claim: 3 years instead of the crucial 2 years from accrual/date of knowledge.
